title: Trajectory slab render mode + narrative announcer for low-fidelity streams
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Introduce a low-fidelity render mode ("trajectory slab") for dense time-series micro-views and an accompanying screen-reader-friendly
' narrative announcer ' that provides concise summaries instead of verbose point-by-point ARIA floods. Target is dashboards with many small sparklines or high-density panels where fidelity can be traded for CPU and frame consistency. This ticket scopes design decisions, acceptance criteria, and handoff artifacts for implementation.

Goals:
- Reduce main-thread time and paint cost for microtimeseries tiles by providing a simplified rendering mode that uses slab aggregation + progressive sampling.
- Provide a short, localizable narrator summary (1-2 lines) that conveys recent trend, last value, and any outlier flags using aria-live polite.
- Ensure keyboard focus, high-contrast token support, and fallback to full-fidelity canvas/SVG when user requests or on large viewports.
- Surface performance telemetry hooks and graceful degradation strategy for older browsers.
acceptance_criteria: Trajectory slab render mode is available as a per-chart flag and via theme tokens for small viewports
Slab rendering reduces composite paint time by >= 40% on representative micro-tiles in the benchmark suite
Narrative announcer emits a localized 1-2 line summary on focus and when new data arrives, using aria-live polite
Keyboard interaction: tab focus lands on a single hotspot per tile; arrow keys move between tiles; Enter toggles full-fidelity view
High-contrast token variants respected (tokens/charting/contrast-high) and colorblind-safe palette applied
Fallback path to SVG/SVG+ARIA exists for environments without OffscreenCanvas or requestIdleCallback
tasks: Consolidate design tokens for micro-viewport mode (spacing, stroke widths, label density)
Define narrative announcer phrasing patterns and localization keys (en, fr, de)
Prototype slab aggregation algorithm and off-main thread paint (Canvas + OffscreenCanvas)
Create keyboard interaction spec and accessible focusable hotspot pattern
Work with Eng to add telemetry spans for render time, paint time, and frame drops
Write component API: enableTrajectorySlab: boolean, announcerConfig: { enabled:boolean, level:string } (doc-level)
Design QA matrix and user testing plan for screen-reader users and low-end devices
comments: 2026-02-16 - Priya Kapoor: Initial proposal posted. Focus on micro-tiles used in Console overview page. Asked ENG to validate OffscreenCanvas availability across supported browsers.
2026-02-18 - Marco Alvarez: Mockups uploaded to Figma; added two token variants (slab-line-width and slab-gap). Prefers 'polite' over 'assertive' for aria-live to avoid interrupting other SR flows.

2026-02-22 - Anika Shah (Eng): Verified OffscreenCanvas availability in Chromium-based browsers; fallback required for Safari/iOS. Suggested using requestAnimationFrame-budgeted progressive rendering for those platforms.

2026-02-25 - Accessibility review (Jamal Rivers): Recommended an aria-hidden data layer for points and a single aria-live summary string. Suggested localizable templates: '{metric} trending {direction}, last {value} at {timestamp}'.
2026-02-28 - Marco Alvarez: Updated interaction spec to include 'Enter toggles full-fidelity' after PM feedback about discoverability.

2026-03-01 - Engineering sync (notes): Agreed to implement slab aggregation in render pipeline and expose a chart prop. ENG-4128 will implement the OffscreenCanvas worker; ENG-4399 will add telemetry hooks. Asked design for microcopy samples and localization keys.

2026-03-04 - Priya Kapoor: Added edge-case guidance: if the user enables 'reduce motion' or 'high-fidelity' via global settings, slab mode must be disabled by default. Added performance target: interactive p95 < 60ms on 2019 Macbook Air equivalent for a 6-column overview row.
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Decision: Use Canvas + OffscreenCanvas for default slab rendering to maximize throughput; fallback to SVG on unsupported browsers to preserve accessibility semantics.
Trade-off: Sacrifice marker-level detail in micro-tiles in favor of stable FPS and lower CPU; full-fidelity accessible on demand.
Decision: Announcer uses templated summaries to minimize verbosity. We will not enumerate every point on every update to avoid SR overload.
qa_plan: Automated visual regression tests for slab vs full mode (pixel tolerance thresholds)
Performance benchmarks on CI using the benchmark harness (desktop/low-end/ci-mobile-emulation)
Manual SR testing with VoiceOver, NVDA, and TalkBack to confirm announcer phrasing and focus sequence
Cross-browser smoke tests to verify OffscreenCanvas fallback path
